homework.title: Part 1: Vocab check (conversation)
homework.instructions: Fill in each blank with a phrase from the word bank. Use each phrase once.
homework.context: Chloe works at a busy coffee shop. Before her shift starts, she catches the owner, Ben.
lines: Chloe
Ben, have you got a minute? I've had an idea I wanted to {run by you}.
Ben
Sure, go ahead.
Chloe

You know how the queue is always really long between seven and nine? A lot of people just give up and leave. I've been {keeping track} this week, and we're losing about thirty customers every morning.
Ben
Thirty? I {didn't realise} it was that many.
Chloe
Yeah. So I was thinking, what if customers could order on their phones before they arrive? They'd just walk in, pick up their coffee and go.
Ben
Interesting. But building an app sounds expensive.
Chloe
We wouldn't need our own app. There are ordering websites that cafés can use for a small monthly fee. I could set it up {in-house}.
Ben
Hmm. Would it really {make a difference}?
Chloe
I think so. It would {free us up} to focus on making drinks instead of taking orders. It might even {cut down on} mistakes, because customers type their own orders.
Ben
What about older customers who don't use their phones much?
Chloe
{That's fair}. They can still order at the counter, like now. That's why I'd like to {start small}, with a one-month trial in the mornings only.
Ben
OK, I think it's {worth a shot}. Send me a few options, and we'll decide by Friday.
Chloe
Great, I'll send them over tonight. Thanks for hearing me out.

homework.title: Part 2: Vocab check (sentences)
homework.instructions: Complete each sentence with a phrase from the box. Use each phrase once. You don't need to change the form of the words.
lines: I'm not sure about the budget yet, but I'll check and {get back to you} by Monday.
OK, it's almost six. Let's {wrap up} and finish the rest tomorrow.

Don't worry about your first week. Anna will {show you the ropes}.
“I hate meetings that run over.” “{I can relate to that}. Ours always finish late.”
Let's try the new schedule for a month and {see how it goes}.
I don't know if we can get a discount from the supplier, but I'll {look into} it.

homework.title: Part 3: Listening
homework.intro: Owen and Jess are friends who work at different companies. They're having lunch together. Listen, then do Parts A and B.

script.text: So, did you talk to your boss about the Friday idea?
I did, yesterday. I was so nervous.
Remind me what you suggested?
That our team could work from home on Fridays. Most of us spend ==over an hour commuting each way==, and on Fridays the office is half empty anyway.
How did you start? Did you just say, "Can we work from home?"
No, I learned from last time. ==I started with the problem. I showed her the results of a quick survey I did.== ==Eight out of ten people said they felt exhausted by Friday because of the commute.==
Smart. What did she say?
At first, she wasn't keen. ==She was worried that clients wouldn't be able to reach us.==
That's fair, to be honest.
Yeah, so I said we'd all keep our phones on, and that one person from the team would always be in the office, ==on a rota==.
Nice. Did she agree?
Not straight away. Then she asked how she'd know people were actually working.
Ha, the classic question.
I know! So I suggested that ==everyone sends a short update at the end of each Friday==, about what they've done and what's left. She liked that.
So it's a yes?
It's a "let's try it". ==Two months, just our team.== After that, she'll check whether our work is still getting done on time.
That's brilliant. Honestly, I'm a bit jealous. My manager would never go for that.
You never know. The trick is to make it easy for them to say yes. ==Start small.==
Maybe I'll run something by her next week, then.
Go for it. ==And bring numbers. Managers love numbers.==

questions.q: Why did Jess suggest working from home on Fridays?
options: Her boss had asked the team for ideas to save money.
People were tired from travelling to and from work.
The office was closed for repairs on Fridays.
questions.why: “Eight out of ten people said they felt exhausted by Friday because of the commute.”

questions.q: How did Jess begin her pitch this time?
options: She asked directly if the team could work from home.
She explained the problem using some data.
She compared her company with other companies.
questions.why: “I started with the problem. I showed her the results of a quick survey I did.”

questions.q: What was the manager's first concern?
options: Clients might not be able to contact the team.
The team would work fewer hours.
The office would be too empty.
questions.why: “She was worried that clients wouldn't be able to reach us.”

questions.q: How did Jess answer the manager's second question?
options: She promised the team would work longer hours.
She offered to call the manager every Friday.
questions.why: “Everyone sends a short update at the end of each Friday, about what they've done and what's left.”

questions.q: What did the manager decide in the end?
options: Everyone in the company can work from home on Fridays.
Jess's team can try it for a limited period.
She'll decide after talking to the clients.
questions.why: “It's a ‘let's try it’. Two months, just our team.”

questions.q: What advice does Jess give Owen?
options: Wait until your manager is in a good mood.
Ask for something small, and support it with figures.
Ask your whole team to pitch the idea together.
questions.why: “Start small.” … “And bring numbers. Managers love numbers.”

homework.title: Part 3B: Complete the summary
homework.instructions: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each blank.
homework.text: Jess wanted her team to work from home on {Fridays|Friday}. In her survey, {eight|8} out of ten people said they felt exhausted because of the {commute}. To deal with her manager's first concern, Jess said one person would always be in the office on a {rota}. The team will also send a short {update} at the end of each Friday. The trial will last {two months|2 months}. Jess's final tip is that managers love {numbers}.

homework.title: Part 4: Speaking (2 minutes)
homework.instructions: Choose ONE option and record yourself speaking for about 2 minutes.

options.title: Pitch an idea to improve your workplace, school or class.
questions: What's the problem? Give a real example or a number.
Imagine someone pushes back. How would you answer?
options.use: Have you got a minute?, You know how…?, I was thinking, what if we…?, It would free us up to…, That way, …, a one-month trial.

options.title: (Story) Tell me about a time you suggested an idea or a change (at work, at school or at home).
questions: What was the problem, and what was your idea?
Who did you talk to, and how did you suggest it?
How did they react? Did they have any worries?
Looking back, would you do anything differently?
options.use: run sth by sb, I'd noticed that…, I was thinking, what if we…?, That's fair, be worth a shot, see how it goes.

options.title: (Pitch) Choose ONE idea below and pitch it to your manager.
choices: Flexible working hours (for example, 8am–4pm instead of 9am–5pm)
Working from home one day a week
A short training course paid for by the company
questions: how it would help the team and the company
one worry your manager might have, and how you'd deal with it: “I know you might be worried that… That's fair, but…”
options.use: You know how…?, What I'm suggesting is…, Nothing too formal, just…, That way, …, keep an eye on, start small.
